title: Johann von Alairt to Prince Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau, Prague 1610-11: upside-down German, deciphered at the time, and an undeciphered slip of November 1611 (catalogue 597)

documents.shelfmark: Landesarchiv Sachsen-Anhalt, Z 44 A 9a Ic Nr. 4 Bd. I, image 400 (fol. 383)
documents.route: unsigned, filed with Johann von Alairt's Prague reports -> Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau

plaintext.source: No gloss; only the receipt docket 'praes. Dessau den 23. Novemb. 1611'

transcription.source: Not yet transcribed; line 1 provisional here, a partial reading by Brackx (issue #128)

documents.shelfmark: Landesarchiv Sachsen-Anhalt, Z 44 A 9a Ic Nr. 1 Bd. II images 152-153, 177, 197, 241-242; Nr. 1 Bd. III images 41-42, 154, 263
documents.route: Johann von Alairt, Prague -> Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment in Kurrent above every cipher line, except the formulas (Brackx; image 241 checked here)

transcription.source: Not yet transcribed; readings of the 18 May letter's opening, date and signature by Brackx (issue #128)

system.summary: German in Latin script with every letter turned top to bottom (b/p, d/q, n/u, m/w trade places; e looks like o, h like y, a like v, i like X, l like j); reflecting a line restores it (Brackx). The prince's own cipher table (sign alphabet and nomenclator 10-70) and a slip nomenclator in the same series are not used by any letter found.
system.sibling_key: Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6 (prince's table) and Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184 (slip key), both unused

prior_solution.where: The 1610 letters were deciphered at the time (interlinear); the Nov 1611 slip has no decipherment. No edition searched for yet.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Michael Brackx searched the series image by image, identified the system and read the slip's first lines with Claude Code; the project owner set up Claude Code and posed the problem.
tools: Brackx's reflection script (issue #128; not in the repository)

solution.what: Brackx (issue #128): Z 44 A 9a Ic is digitised further than the catalogue row said (Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-IV, Nr. 3, Nr. 4 Bd. I, Nr. 5, Nr. 6); image URL pattern found.
Brackx described the prince's cipher table (Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6) and a slip nomenclator (Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184); searched about 2,280 images for letters using them; none found.
Brackx identified Alairt's cipher as German written upside down; reflected lines of the 18 May 1610 letter read as German and agree with the interlinear decipherment (date line, opening).

Here: images 6, 241 and 400 fetched; the table is as described; image 241 flipped top to bottom gives Latin-script German with o for e under the dark gloss; slip line 1 transcribed and read as 'Will der Kayser bericht werden, dass der Hertz-', agreeing with Brackx.

outcome.method_basis: The system is identified and the 1610 letters carry decipherments of the time, but nothing is transcribed or measured yet; the Nov 1611 slip, the one undeciphered piece, is read only in its first lines.

gaps.detail: eight lines; workable by reflection; Brackx asked for his reading (issue #128)

gaps.item: 1610 letters: decipherments not transcribed or checked against the cipher lines
gaps.detail: seven letters, images listed in NOTES.md

gaps.item: Nr. 2 Bd. III-IV, Nr. 5-6, Nr. 1 Bd. III image 80 not searched for letters in the prince's table

credits.note: searched the series image by image, identified Alairt's upside-down cipher and the undeciphered Nov 1611 slip, described both keys (with Claude Code)
